channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Brasil anuncia US$ 100 milhões anuais para fundo do Mercosul
item.description: Brazil announced it will allocate US$100 million annually to the Structural Convergence Fund of Mercosul (Focem), reinforcing its commitment to reducing inequalities among member states. The announcement was made by Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira during the CMC meeting in Asunción and will be formalized by President Lula at the Mercosul Summit. The fund finances infrastructure projects such as roads, energy, and sanitation, with Brazil currently contributing around 70% of the total resources.

item.title: O impacto da crise familiar: Como a ala ideológica reagiu ao atrito entre Michelle e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Influencers Paulo Figueiredo and Oswaldo Eustáquio publicly exposed the rift between Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro, intensifying a family crisis that is fracturing the ideological base of Bolsonarism. The statements deepened the split within the digital militia, with radical opposition sectors exploiting the conflict to undermine the movement's cohesion.

item.title: Quem são os brasileiros que prometem não votar neste ano, segundo nova pesquisa
item.description: A Nexus/BTG Pactual poll released on June 29, 2026, shows that 3% of Brazilian voters say they have decided not to vote in the October 4 first-round elections, with higher rates among women (4%), those aged 60 or older (4%), voters with only elementary education (4%), evangelicals (6%), those earning up to one minimum wage (4%), and residents of the Southeast (4%). In 2022, over 32 million voters abstained in the first round, or 20.9% of the electorate. The survey interviewed 2,009 voters between July 26 and 28, with a two-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Michelle deixa de seguir Carluxo e Eduardo nas redes
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro unfollowed her brother-in-law Carlos Bolsonaro and her brother Eduardo Bolsonaro on social media after sharing a June 24 video in which she described being treated with hostility by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during a discussion about political formation. The move suggests a possible rift within the Bolsonaro family, with potential implications for the group's political cohesion ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: CNJ divulga ranking de transparência e 20 órgãos do Judiciário atingem nota máxima
item.description: In 2026, 20 Brazilian Judiciary bodies achieved the maximum score in the CNJ's Transparency Ranking, up from 19 in the previous edition. These include seven state justice tribunals, seven regional labor tribunals, four regional electoral tribunals, the TRF-2, and the CSJT. The CNJ itself scored 96.3%, while four bodies fell below 90%, with TRT10 at the lowest with 86.6%. The ranking evaluates 83 questions across 11 themes, and bodies have five days to appeal scores before the final results are published.

item.title: Valdemar defende Michelle na eleição após atrito com Flávio
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, met with Michelle Bolsonaro to address the fallout from a video in which she accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of mistreatment. The meeting aims to reinforce her support for the party in the 2026 elections following internal tensions within the Bolsonaro clan. Valdemar acknowledged uncertainty about the electoral outcome but seeks to preserve party unity.

item.title: Com atritos na família, Michelle deixa de seguir Carlos e Eduardo
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro unfollowed her stepsons Eduardo and Carlos Bolsonaro on Instagram after posting videos in which she said she felt humiliated and stabbed in the back by her stepson, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president. Despite an apology from Flávio and mediation efforts by the PL party, Michelle maintained the unfollow of Eduardo and Carlos while still following Flávio, as Eduardo publicly criticized her on X. The family rift also included Michelle posting biblical verses seemingly referencing the situation.

item.title: Presidenciáveis celebram vitória do Brasil; Flávio Bolsonaro usa número de Martinelli e Lula posa com Janja
item.description: Presidential pre-candidates celebrated Brazil's victory over Japan in the 2026 World Cup. Flávio Bolsonaro linked Martinelli's goal (wearing number 22) to the PL party's ballot number, while Lula posed with Janja and ministers wearing the Brazilian Paralympic Committee jacket. Other candidates, such as Romeu Zema and Renan Santos, also commented on the match, tying it to political narratives.

item.title: CNJ lança ferramenta de IA para identificar litigância abusiva
item.description: The CNJ announced the launch of Atalaia, an AI tool to identify patterns of abusive litigation in the judiciary, with presentation scheduled for June 30, 2026. The system cross-references data from various courts to detect repetitive, standardized, or weakly documented actions, serving as a support tool for judges without replacing their decision. The initiative reflects the growing use of AI in the Brazilian judiciary, with 66% of courts having AI projects under development in 2023, according to a CNJ survey.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026: 'Perfis fantasmas' impulsionam conteúdos pagos contra Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A report reveals that fake social media profiles are being used to amplify paid content attacking Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 elections. This strategy aims to artificially create a negative perception of the candidate through disinformation and algorithmic manipulation. Digital platforms are under investigation for potential electoral law violations and improper data use.

item.title: Republicanos avalia punição a Manga após vídeo em sede do União Brasil em Sorocaba
item.description: The Republicans party is considering punishing Sorocaba's mayor, Rodrigo Manga, after he posted a social media video showing the União Brasil headquarters decorated with his photo and that of his wife, Sirlange Maganhato, a federal deputy candidate for União Brasil. National party president Marcos Pereira said there is a strong internal movement due to a clear sense of betrayal, as Manga was elected and re-elected under the Republicans banner. Manga said he was unaware of the dissatisfaction, reaffirmed his respect for Pereira, support for his wife’s candidacy, and stated he has no intention of leaving the party, despite facing judicial proceedings for corruption, money laundering, and fraud tied to Operation Copia e Cola.

item.title: Vieira: Mercosul é "baluarte de liberdade" em meio ao protecionismo
item.description: Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira stated that Mercosul is a 'bulwark of liberty' amid global protectionism, emphasizing its role in promoting trade and free movement of people. He warned against unilateral initiatives undermining the spirit of the Treaty of Asunción and advocated for a transparent, equitable distribution of EU-Mercosul tariff quotas that do not deprive the bloc's productive sectors of their benefits.

item.title: Irmãos Bolsonaro devem responder por incentivarem atos típicos de guerra contra o Brasil
item.description: The article argues that brothers Eduardo and Flávio Bolsonaro could be held legally accountable under Law 14.197/2021 for incentivating acts typical of war against Brazil by supporting U.S. policies such as tariffs and designating criminal factions as terrorists. These actions allegedly constitute negotiation with a foreign government to harm the democratic rule of law, with penalties potentially doubled if belligerent consequences follow.

item.title: Jogou Bem ou Jogou Mal? Heróis da classificação, Martinelli e Bruno Guimarães são eleitos os melhores; Paquetá é o pior
item.description: Gabriel Martinelli was voted Brazil's best player against Japan with 94.31% approval after scoring the winning goal in the 50th minute of the second half. Bruno Guimarães ranked second with 89.16% for the assist, while Lucas Paquetá received the worst rating at 33.78% due to an injury that forced his substitution at halftime. Despite the positive result, the 'Jogou Bem ou Jogou Mal' voting remains open for GLOBO readers.

item.title: DC quer lançar ator Humberto Martins e filha de Roberto Jefferson para deputado federal no Rio
item.description: The Christian Democracy (DC) party plans to launch actor Humberto Martins and Cristiane Brasil, daughter of Roberto Jefferson, as federal deputy candidates for Rio de Janeiro in the 2026 elections, according to Folha de S.Paulo. The strategy aims to leverage the public visibility of these figures to strengthen the party's ticket in the state.

item.title: Lula comemora vitória do Brasil contra o Japão: "Parabéns à Seleção"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated Brazil’s 2-1 victory over Japan in the World Cup, praising the team’s effort and expressing national pride. He watched the match at the Palácio da Alvorada with First Lady Janja and government ministers. Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro highlighted the coincidence that the goal scorers wore jerseys numbered 13 and 22 — matching the ballot numbers of the PT and PL — using it to criticize Lula on social media.

item.title: Michelle deixa de seguir Eduardo e Carlos Bolsonaro após crise pública com Flávio
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro unfollowed her sons Eduardo and Carlos Bolsonaro on social media after accusing them of coordinating with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in public attacks against her. The conflict began when Michelle advocated for Priscila Costa’s Senate candidacy in Ceará, which was overridden by an alliance involving André Fernandes and figures linked to Ciro Gomes, which she viewed as a familial betrayal.

item.title: Na véspera de reunião de cúpula, Mercosul mostra apoio a presidente da Bolívia após semanas de protestos que paralisaram o país
item.description: Mercosul foreign ministers voiced strong support for Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz following seven weeks of road blockades and protests that caused shortages of food, fuel, and medicine. The statement came ahead of the bloc's presidential summit in Asunción, where leaders will begin negotiations on an economic association agreement with Japan. Paraguayan Chancellor Rubén Ramírez stressed that democratic stability and constitutional order are shared Mercosul principles, condemning the violence and attempts to undermine Bolivia's constitutional order.

item.title: Janja participa de encontro com católicos em Brasília
item.description: First Lady Rosângela da Silva, known as Janja, will attend the National Catholic Meeting of the PT in Brasília on June 30 at the party’s national headquarters. The event will bring together PT activists and religious leaders to discuss Brazil’s challenges, faith, and democracy, featuring participants such as Benedictine monk Marcelo Barros and Franciscan friar Frei Davi, along with PT leaders Edinho Silva, Gilberto Carvalho, and Gleide Andrade. Janja’s participation reflects the PT’s strategy to strengthen dialogue with religious electorates, particularly Catholics and Evangelicals, following her engagements with Evangelical women in early June.

item.title: Hablla leva debate sobre IA e WhatsApp à América Latina
item.description: Hablla completed in June 2026 the Conversational Growth Experience, a series of in-person events officially supported by Meta across ten Brazilian cities and Montevideo, attracting over 2,000 participants. The initiative revealed that while WhatsApp is Brazil’s primary commercial channel, most companies use it without structure, governance, or metrics, leading to missed opportunities. As a Meta-certified BSP tier Select processing over 30 million monthly conversations, Hablla advocates for a professionalized architecture to optimize commercial use of WhatsApp.

item.title: Lula e Janja comemoram vitória brasileira sobre a seleção do Japão
item.description: President Lula and First Lady Janja celebrated Brazil's 2-1 victory over Japan in the 2026 World Cup in Houston, which secured the team's advancement to the round of 16. Lula wore a jacket from Brazil's Paralympic team at the Paris 2024 Games during the match. The text also includes an explanatory note stating that the World Cup is a private, for-profit event organized by FIFA, and that Brazil's team is selected by the CBF, a private entity with no government affiliation.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cala frente a ataque de conselheiro a voto feminino, e ato com mulheres vira teatro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's presidential pre-candidate, faces growing rejection among female voters due to his silence amid misogynistic attacks by his advisor Paulo Figueiredo, who claimed 'women vote very poorly'. Despite attempting to organize a meeting with female leaders, Michelle Bolsonaro and Damares Alves are expected to absent themselves, leaving the event without meaningful representation and reinforcing the perception that the candidate is alienating the female vote, which constitutes 53% of the electorate.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cala diante de ataque de conselheiro a voto feminino e ato com mulheres vira teatro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL's presidential pre-candidate, remains silent amid sexist attacks by his advisor Paulo Figueiredo, who claimed women 'vote very badly' and posted an offensive sign. His silence is interpreted as consent, reflected in a 58% rejection rate among female voters in a Nexus/BTG poll. A planned meeting with female leaders for Wednesday is likely to fail, as Michelle Bolsonaro and Damares Alves have not confirmed attendance, leaving the event with only radical bolsonarist support, which risks alienating independent female voters.

item.title: Michelle se choca com o purosanguismo bolsonarista
item.description: The text analyzes internal tensions within post-2022 Bolsonarism, highlighting the leadership struggle between Jair Bolsonaro’s sons and Michelle Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro is portrayed as the ‘pure-blood’ heir chosen to perpetuate the family legacy, while Michelle, lacking Bolsonaro blood, is seen as an outsider and threat to the hereditary power project. The narrative suggests that Jair’s sons, including Eduardo, would unite to neutralize Michelle, safeguarding the family’s political patrimony.

item.title: Milei recibe a Flávio Bolsonaro en Buenos Aires y anuncia que no irá a la cumbre del Mercosur
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei received Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro and 2026 presidential candidate, in Buenos Aires, announcing his support for the rise of the 'blue tide' far-right movement in Latin America. Milei also confirmed he will not attend the Mercosur summit in Paraguay, avoiding a direct meeting with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, thereby reinforcing his alliance with Brazil's opposition.

item.title: Aposta de Lula para o governo de Minas, Marília Campos chama ex-tucano Gabriel Azevedo de governador
item.description: Marília Campos, former mayor of Contagem and PT’s pré-candidate for the Senate, praised Gabriel Azevedo (MDB), a pré-candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, calling him 'governor' during a meeting with political leaders from Northern Minas Gerais. She reiterated that she will only run if it’s for the Senate, despite pressure from Lula and the PT to run for governor. The meeting also included Jarbas Soares (PSB), another gubernatorial pré-candidate, sparking speculation about a possible broad front or PT support for Azevedo or Soares if Marília declines Lula’s request.

item.title: Após vitória do Brasil contra o Japão, Flávio tenta capitalizar com camisa de Martinelli e Lula celebra avanço da Seleção
item.description: Brazil's 2-1 victory over Japan, secured by Gabriel Martinelli's goal wearing the number 22 jersey, was quickly leveraged by 2026 presidential pre-candidates for political messaging. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) linked Martinelli's jersey number to his party's electoral number (22), while President Lula celebrated the team's advancement and Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema used humor and memes comparing Brazilian barbecue to Japanese sushi. The PL party reinforced the number 22 symbolism, sparking debate over the politicization of sports.

item.title: “O 22 salvou o Brasil”, diz Flávio ao comemorar gol de Martinelli
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated Gabriel Martinelli's goal (wearing number 22) in Brazil's win over Japan at the 2026 World Cup, linking the number 22 to his party, the PL, and claiming 'the 22 saved Brazil'. The PL also posted on social media: 'Once again, 22 saves Brazil', implying a political omen. Brazil won 2-1 and advanced to the round of 16.

item.title: Fora da campanha, Marinho mantém o diálogo do governo com transportadores no RS
item.description: Labor and Employment Minister Luiz Marinho (PT) attended a dinner with approximately 200 automobile transporters (truckers) in Flores da Cunha (RS), maintaining dialogue between the federal government and the sector despite not being part of Lula’s campaign team. The meeting took place on the eve of the 2026 electoral period, aiming to preserve institutional communication channels.

item.title: Apresentadores de rádio e TV que querem disputar eleição têm até 30 de junho para deixarem emissoras
item.description: Radio and TV presenters must leave their stations by June 30 to run in the 2026 elections, as required by TSE rules. Among those who have stepped down are Silvia Abravanel (PSD, SP), Sikêra Júnior (Republicans, SP), and José Luiz Datena (PSB, SP). Parties are also strengthening their slates with digital influencers, such as Gracyanne Barbosa (Republicans, RJ), Val Marchiori (Republicans, SP), and Rico Melquiades (PSDB, AL).

item.title: Nova líder do governo no Senado se reúne com Lula para alinhar estratégia de atuação
item.description: Senator Teresa Leitão, the new government leader in the Senate, met with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Minister José Guimarães to align the government's strategy in Congress. This was their first meeting since she assumed the role, aimed at defining the next steps of the government's legislative agenda.

item.title: Lula faz primeira reunião com a nova líder do governo no Senado
item.description: President Lula held his first meeting with the new government leader in the Senate, Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), who replaced Jaques Wagner in the role. During the meeting, they aligned on the government’s priority agenda in the Upper House and discussed next steps for advancing key legislative priorities. The encounter underscores the effort to strengthen coordination between the Planalto and Congress to advance the government’s reform agenda and strategic projects.

item.title: “Foi o 22 que salvou o Brasil”, diz Flávio após gol de Martinelli
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for the presidency, celebrated Gabriel Martinelli's winning goal in Brazil's victory over Japan at the World Cup, linking the number 22 on the striker's jersey to the number of his party, the PL. He said 'it was the 22 that saved Brazil,' using the sporting feat as a political metaphor to reinforce his party identity. The statement was made after the match and reported by O Antagonista.

item.title: Autoexilado nos EUA, Eduardo vai a jogo do Brasil no Texas
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro, former federal deputy self-exiled in the U.S. since February 2025, posted on Instagram that he attended Brazil’s 2-1 World Cup win over Japan in Houston, Texas. He was seen with sports journalist Thiago Asmar (Pilhado) and wrote 'Saudades…' in a video of the teams’ flags on the field. Eduardo was sentenced by the STF in June 2026 to 4 years and 2 months in prison for coercion in his father’s trial, became ineligible, and lost his federal police position, though he rejects the ruling.

item.title: Políticos comemoram classificação da seleção brasileira contra o Japão
item.description: Politicians from various parties celebrated Brazil's 2-1 victory over Japan in the 2026 World Cup, highlighting Gabriel Martinelli's goal wearing the number 22 jersey and drawing symbolic links to the PL party's number. While some praised the result and used the match for political mobilization, others like Erika Hilton and Renan Santos criticized the refereeing. STF Minister Flávio Dino stated the team must reduce reliance on individual brilliance and develop a more structural, collective style of play.

item.title: Cientista político vê um risco no tom do discurso que Flávio Bolsonaro usou na Argentina
item.description: Political scientist Marcos Teixeira warns that Flávio Bolsonaro’s strategy of radicalizing his rhetoric and intensifying international agendas may solidify support among hardline bolsonarists but hurt his chances with moderate and undecided voters, who are decisive in national elections. While understandable after the Banco Master scandal, this shift risks alienating the center—the very bloc needed to win. Regarding Lula, Teixeira says his main problem remains communication: his public statements often create unnecessary backlash due to a lack of restraint.

item.title: Lula se reúne com Teresa Leitão após senadora assumir liderança do governo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with Senator Teresa Leitão, the new government leader in the Senate, to discuss the government's priority agenda, including the PECs on ending the 6x1 work scale and public security. Leitão emphasized her goal to strengthen articulation between the Planalto Palace, the allied base, and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to advance government proposals. The meeting followed the removal of Jaques Wagner from the Senate leadership role due to the Federal Police's Operation Compliance Zero.

item.title: Joaquim Barbosa não decola e DC segue sem data para oficializar pré-candidatura
item.description: Joaquim Barbosa, former STF minister and DC's pre-candidate, has only 1% voting intention in the Nexus/BTG poll, trailing behind Lula (42%), Flávio Bolsonaro (34%), and other contenders. The party has not yet set a date to officially launch his candidacy, attempting to form a coalition with parties like PSDB, MDB, Podemos, and Republicans to strengthen his bid — without success so far.

item.title: Pesquisa traz alívio para Flávio, mas não mede efeitos de nova crise, diz cientista político
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula leading with 42% in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 34%, signaling a one-point recovery for the senator after the Banco Master scandal. In the runoff simulation, Lula holds 47% versus Flávio’s 44%. Political scientist Marcos Teixeira notes that Flávio’s decline may have stalled, suggesting the initial impact of the scandal has been absorbed, but warns that the fallout from the Michelle Bolsonaro feud remains unmeasured, keeping the race deeply polarized.

item.title: Dirceu publica foto de Lula e Brizola assistindo a jogo da Copa de 98
item.description: Former minister José Dirceu (PT) posted a historical photo on Instagram showing Lula and Leonel Brizola watching a 1998 World Cup match, emphasizing the unity of Brazilian left-wing leaders defending national sovereignty. He referenced the 1998 'União do Povo Muda Brasil' coalition, where Lula ran for president and Brizola as vice, though defeated in the first round by Fernando Henrique Cardoso. The post coincided with Brazil's 2-1 victory over Japan in the 2026 World Cup, securing a place in the round of 16.

item.title: DC planeja lançar ex-global e filha de Roberto Jefferson à Câmara
item.description: The Christian Democracy (DC) party plans to nominate actor Humberto Martins and Cristiane Brasil, daughter of former deputy Roberto Jefferson, as candidates for the Chamber of Deputies in the 2026 elections. The party is also trying to convince Marlene Mattos, former manager of Xuxa, to run for federal deputy from Rio de Janeiro. DC aims to expand its federal caucus with well-known figures from entertainment and conservative politics.

item.title: Paquetá sai de campo amparado pelos companheiros após fim do 1º tempo
item.description: Lucas Paquetá suffered a thigh injury and took a blow to the face during the first half of Brazil's match against Japan in the 2026 World Cup. He was assisted by teammates and left the pitch limping, carried by Neymar and Endrick toward the locker room. Brazil faces Japan in the second round, with the winner advancing to the round of 16.

item.title: Moraes vai decidir se tira Bolsonaro da prisão domiciliar depois de receber advogados no STF
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes will meet with Jair Bolsonaro's lawyers on Tuesday to decide whether to maintain the former president under house arrest, after the humanitarian period expired. The decision hinges on an investigation into whether one of Bolsonaro's security guards illegally possessed a firearm owned by the ex-president, which prosecutors consider a serious violation. Bolsonaro's defense claims the weapon was being taken for repair and that his health remains critically poor.

item.title: Eduardo Bolsonaro volta a assistir jogo da seleção nos EUA
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro, former federal deputy and son of ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, was seen attending the Brazil vs Japan match at Houston's stadium in Texas, part of the World Cup. He shared on social media a record of his arrival at the stadium, accompanied by journalist Thiago Asmar. This marks the second recent occasion he has followed the Brazilian national team in the United States.

item.title: Gaeco Nacional amplia atuação para crimes eleitorais de facções
item.description: The National Gaeco has been expanded to handle electoral crimes committed by criminal organizations, per a June 2026 resolution by the MPF Superior Council. The new jurisdiction covers related offenses under Federal or Electoral Court jurisdiction, excluding STJ and STF cases unless the PGR requests otherwise. The coordinator may petition the STJ to transfer cases from State to Federal Court when deemed appropriate.

item.title: Governo envia projeto para elevar o teto de faturamento do MEI
item.description: The Lula government has submitted a bill to the Chamber of Deputies proposing to raise the annual revenue cap for Microentrepreneur Individual (MEI) to BRL 110,000 in 2027 and BRL 140,000 in 2028, up from the current BRL 81,000 set in 2018. The proposal, negotiated during the debate on ending the 6×1 work scale, would also allow MEIs to hire more than one employee, expanding their job creation potential. Chamber President Hugo Motta confirmed receipt of the bill and emphasized its significance as a pro-small business measure in an election year, expected to face little opposition in Congress.

item.title: Lula propõe reajuste escalonado do MEI para R$ 140 mil em 2028
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) sent a bill to the Chamber of Deputies proposing a staggered increase in the annual revenue cap for MEI (Individual Microentrepreneur), raising the limit from R$80,000 to R$110,000 in 2027 and R$140,000 in 2028. The measure aims to expand access to the simplified tax regime for small businesses.

item.title: Lula envia PL que amplia teto do MEI para R$ 110 mil em 2027
item.description: President Lula has sent to Congress a bill proposing to raise the MEI's annual revenue cap from R$81,000 to R$110,000 in 2027 and R$140,000 in 2028, while allowing up to two employees per business. The measure, part of negotiations tied to PEC 6 X 1, aims to promote formalization and growth of microentrepreneurs, though it entails fiscal renunciation and increased pressure on other taxpayers. The government also announced complementary initiatives such as Contrata+ Brasil and Pé no Futuro, developed with sectoral ministries, to expand MEI participation in public procurement and provide entrepreneurial training and seed funding for youth not entering higher education.

item.title: Lula entrega a Motta projeto para ampliar limite do MEI
item.description: President Lula delivered to Chamber President Hugo Motta a bill proposing to increase the annual revenue limit for MEI microentrepreneurs from R$81,000 to R$110,000 in 2027 and R$140,000 in 2028, while also allowing the hiring of more employees. The measure aims to strengthen small businesses and encourage formalization in the sector.

item.title: O desconhecimento sobre investigação que mira ligação de Jaques Wagner com Vorcaro
item.description: The Federal Police operation investigating Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) over alleged financial ties to a former associate of banker Daniel Vorcaro remains largely unknown to the public, with only 27% saying they are well-informed. Lula and Bolsonaro voters are the most engaged, while 'non-polarized' voters show the greatest detachment, with 30% never having heard of the case. The Nexus survey, conducted June 26–28, 2026 with 2,009 respondents, has a 2-point margin of error and is registered with the TSE under BR-08521/2026.
